name: Lebanon
headline: Lebanon: +4.0% growth in 2025, 14.6% inflation, debt 139% of GDP
sections: Lebanon is a $34.5 billion economy (2025), the world's 113th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.0% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $12K at purchasing-power parity (2024), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 1.4% of GDP (2021).

Consumer prices rose 14.6% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, down from 171.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 11.5% (2023), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 22.7% (2023).
Gross government debt is 139% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 158% in 2020. The general government balance is +3.3% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is −22.5% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 82% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 6.8% of GDP (2024).
Life expectancy is 77.9 years (2024). Population: 5.8 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
